paragraph: **Yes, for soil-moisture drought on the test that counts, with conditions.** On the pre-registered, one-time fresh test (144 regions never used in development, target months 2025-01 to 2026-09), the Bi-LSTM beat logistic regression on current-month VCI at estimating the current month's drought (job 1). The residual Bi-LSTM, chosen in development, scored AUC 0.659 against LR's 0.621: a difference of +0.038 [+0.020, +0.057] that passed the rule fixed in advance. The plain Bi-LSTM, added after the development results, scored +0.042 [+0.024, +0.060]. The gain is not an artifact of the FLDAS label: scored against an independent soil-moisture model (NLDAS-2), the residual Bi-LSTM still leads LR by +0.027 [+0.013, +0.041]. It is a qualified yes for seven reasons. (1) In development (four folds over 2016-2023) the same networks lost to LR by about 0.05. Across the folds and the fresh test, their gap to LR follows the amount of training data: from -0.114 at 323K training windows to +0.042 at 1.12M. The learning curve says it is years of record that matter, not windows: on two folds, going from two to five training years narrowed the Bi-LSTM's gap from -0.067 to -0.028, and it was still narrowing from four to five years (+0.008 [+0.004, +0.014]), as were the gaps of the CNN + Bi-LSTM and the VCI-only Bi-LSTM; eight times as many training windows from more regions narrowed none of them. That fits the Bi-LSTM needing all eight years to win, although a straight-line extension of the curve reaches only about zero at eight years, so the years alone may not account for the whole fresh-test gain. (2) The test is one 21-month, unusually dry period (39.5% of windows in drought), and region resampling does not show how much another period would differ. (3) The GRU and the residual Bi-LSTM score within 0.006 AUC of the plain Bi-LSTM, so the evidence favours a recurrent network on the full monthly inputs, not the Bi-LSTM in particular. (4) The gain needs the NDVI level and spread, clear-fraction and season inputs: the VCI-only Bi-LSTM gains less, and per-pixel VCI image tiles add nothing. (5) It does not extend to the missing-month job (no detectable difference) or to forecasting drought onset (every model near chance). (6) It is specific to soil-moisture drought: against climatic drought, LR on VCI ranks drought better. With SPEI over 180 days (Phase 6's choice), the residual Bi-LSTM trails LR by -0.030 [-0.047, -0.012]; with SPEI over 270 days it trails too, and with SPEI over 90 days they tie. (7) Under realistic single-view sampling the gain shrinks. With a pass every 7 days, the residual Bi-LSTM and the GRU keep about +0.02 AUC. At 32 days the gain is gone, and the plain Bi-LSTM is the least robust. The saved models reproduce their scored predictions, and the fresh test was scored once and is locked.
